claims.text: Hexagonal architecture, also called ports and adapters, keeps the business rules in a core that reaches the outside only through interfaces the core declares itself (ports), each implemented outside the core by adapters.

At stage-1 OrderService takes IOrderRepository and INotifier; PlaceOrderAsync calls repository.AddAsync(order), then SaveChangesAsync(), then notifier.Send(order.Id, "order placed"); OrderService names no logging, PostgreSQL or EF Core type.
IOrderRepository (DonHang.Domain) declares FindAsync, ListByCustomerAsync, AddAsync, SaveChangesAsync; INotifier (DonHang.Domain) declares one method, void Send(int orderId, string subject).

EfOrderRepository implements IOrderRepository with EF Core and PostgreSQL; LoggingNotifier implements INotifier with logger.LogInformation; in DonHang.Tests FakeOrderRepository uses a Dictionary<int, Order>, FakeNotifier a List of sent (OrderId, Subject).
LoggingNotifier.cs starts with using DonHang.Domain; and using Microsoft.Extensions.Logging;. No file in DonHang.Domain names LoggingNotifier, EfOrderRepository or FakeOrderRepository.
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: LoggingNotifier.cs:1-2; git grep -e LoggingNotifier -e EfOrderRepository -e FakeOrderRepository -- DonHang.Domain (no match)

claims.text: Order and OrderItem in DonHang.Domain/Entities.cs are plain classes with properties and carry no attribute (no EF Core attribute).

DonHangDbContext.OnModelCreating maps Order to orders and OrderItem to order_items (ToTable), each property to a column (HasColumnName), relationships via foreign keys (HasMany/HasOne ... HasForeignKey), and the composite key of order_items (HasKey).
claims.source_hint: examples/don-hang @ stage-1: DonHangDbContext.cs:38-57; EF Core docs: Modeling, table mapping (ToTable), column names (HasColumnName), keys (HasKey)

claims.text: LoggingNotifier is registered as the INotifier in ServiceCollectionExtensions (AddScoped<INotifier, LoggingNotifier>), so a text message means a new INotifier implementation registered there instead; OrderService, the entities and both interfaces stay unchanged.

The hexagon is only the usual drawing (core in the middle, ports on its edges, adapters around it); the number of sides has no meaning; what makes a design hexagonal is that adapters depend on the core's ports.
If IOrderRepository moved to DonHang.Infrastructure, DonHang.Domain would need a ProjectReference to that project to name it, breaking the dependency rule.

At stage-1, `git grep -n -e ": IOrderRepository" -e ": INotifier" -- "DonHang.*/*.cs"` prints four lines (EfOrderRepository.cs:7, LoggingNotifier.cs:9, FakeNotifier.cs:6, FakeOrderRepository.cs:8); the grep of DonHang.Domain for the three adapter names prints nothing.
